schema_note: Base fields are verbatim from repo avatar-stack/freedom/scene_job.example.json. Fields added by the gpu-4090 pack: packs, pipeline, and per-character/per-segment reference_pack / video_pack / view blocks. They are additive and change no base field.
purpose: The planned first freedom test: two characters, free-text segments, one living background. Wispkin drifts in tilting its mask, then performs Dark Wave; Dorowani hops forward, charges a Water Orb, and pushes it out.

packs.clarification: Owner clarification, 2026-10-28 — read before authoring or running any job.

reference_packs.contents: Different views, angles and perspectives per character. NOT single-view.
reference_packs.role: Source of truth for what a character looks like from any view. The still for a view is the source every moving version of that view is built from.
reference_packs.location: repo reference-packs/ (per-character pack manifest names the actual still files; paths + sha256 are filled in per character at authoring time and hash-checked in preflight — they are not guessed in this example)

video_packs.limitation: Only one view per character today. This limitation belongs to the VIDEO packs only — do not state it about the reference packs.

packs.view_sourcing_rule: A video pack gains an extra view FROM the reference-pack stills: build the moving version from the still for that view. Never generate a view from nothing; never let the video model invent a view.

pipeline.method: Owner-locked: generate each character separately (same scene prompt + timing map) -> frame-1 + likeness gate -> chain segments -> cut out background -> overlay on the living background plate -> post (contact shadows at composite time only, then grade).

generation.input_image: the reference-pack still for the segment's required view (see each segment's view block)

gates: likeness_gate.py (per generated segment) — a clip without its gate packet is not reportable and is never composited

cutout.primary: white_matte.py (repo avatar-stack project code — primary for flat cartoon plates)
cutout.backup: BiRefNet (MIT) — backup, and the working option for non-white-field plates

pipeline.composite: freedom/scene_composite.py over the living background plate in this job's background block (never the still plate)
pipeline.post: shadows first (drawn at composite time — character art never carries a baked shadow), then one grade over the composite

background.note: The living Gate background, life-proof v1 (cloud-shadow drift, leaf drift, pollen, wind bed) - the current living version of the Gate piece for this scene, per the parts-catalog current-version marks. NOT the v1 still plate.

segments.action: Wispkin drifts slowly across the frame from left to right, bobbing gently on its smoky trail, tilting its cracked white skull mask side to side as if listening to something far away

view.source_still: AUTHORING-TIME: path + sha256 of the reference-pack still for required_view; generation starts from this still and preflight hash-checks it
view.sourcing_rule: from the reference-pack still — never generated from nothing
